details:
Orbit Guard – AI-Powered Space Waste Detection, Tracking and Collision Risk Monitoring System

1. Abstract

Orbit Guard is an AI-powered space monitoring system designed to detect, classify, track, and monitor space debris orbiting Earth. Space debris, also known as space junk, includes inactive satellites, abandoned rocket parts, broken spacecraft components, and small fragments. These objects create serious risks for operational satellites, space stations, astronauts, and future space missions.

Orbit Guard uses Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and orbital tracking technologies to identify and monitor space debris. It collects satellite orbital information from available datasets, analyzes object characteristics, and classifies different types of orbital objects.

The system also provides orbit visualization and collision-risk monitoring features to identify potentially dangerous close approaches between objects. An interactive web dashboard displays satellite locations, debris information, orbital paths, and warning notifications.

The main objective of Orbit Guard is to improve space safety, support satellite monitoring, and contribute to reducing the risks associated with increasing space pollution.

2. Introduction

Space technology plays an important role in modern life. Satellites are used for communication, navigation, weather forecasting, television broadcasting, and scientific research. However, the increasing number of satellite launches has resulted in growing space pollution.

Space debris consists of artificial objects orbiting Earth that are no longer useful. These objects include inactive satellites, abandoned rocket stages, and broken spacecraft components.

Even small debris fragments can damage operational satellites because objects in orbit travel at extremely high speeds. Collisions can also generate additional debris, increasing the problem.

Orbit Guard aims to address this challenge by developing an intelligent monitoring platform that combines AI, orbital data analysis, and interactive visualization to identify space debris and monitor potential collision risks.

3. Problem Statement

The increasing amount of space debris is becoming a major challenge for space organizations and satellite operators. Monitoring thousands of orbital objects and predicting their movements requires continuous tracking and complex calculations.

Traditional monitoring systems depend on specialized infrastructure and expert analysis. Therefore, an accessible and intelligent system is needed to identify orbital objects, track their movements, and estimate potential collision risks.

Orbit Guard proposes an AI-powered platform that simplifies space debris monitoring through automated classification, orbital visualization, and collision-risk alerts.

4. Objectives

  • To detect and classify space debris using AI and Machine Learning.
  • To collect and analyze satellite orbital information.
  • To track the positions and movements of orbital objects.
  • To visualize satellites and debris using a 3D Earth model.
  • To estimate potential collision risks.
  • To generate alerts for potentially dangerous close approaches.
  • To provide a user-friendly monitoring dashboard.
  • To support space safety and environmental sustainability.

5. Proposed System

The proposed Orbit Guard system combines Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, orbital mechanics, and web technologies.

First, the system collects orbital data from available satellite tracking sources. The collected information is processed using Python and stored in a database.

Next, a machine-learning model analyzes available object characteristics and classifies orbital objects into categories such as active satellites, inactive satellites, rocket bodies, and debris.

The orbital tracking module estimates object positions and displays their movements around Earth. A collision-risk analysis module compares predicted positions to identify potentially dangerous close approaches.

Finally, the system generates notifications and displays the results through an interactive dashboard.

7. Main Modules

Module 1: Data Collection

This module collects satellite and orbital information from available datasets and APIs. It stores object IDs, satellite names, orbital parameters, and other tracking details for further analysis.

Module 2: AI-Based Object Classification

This module uses Machine Learning to classify orbital objects into categories such as active satellites, inactive satellites, rocket bodies, and space debris. The model analyzes available object characteristics and historical datasets to identify different object types.

Module 3: Orbit Visualization

This module displays orbital objects using an interactive 3D Earth model. Users can view satellite positions, debris locations, orbital paths, and object information. Three.js can be used to create the visualization.

Module 4: Collision Risk Detection

This module analyzes the predicted positions of selected orbital objects to identify potentially dangerous close approaches. It estimates the separation distance and approach time and assigns Low, Medium, or High risk categories based on configured criteria.

A close approach does not automatically mean a collision. Reliable collision probability requires orbital uncertainty analysis.

Module 5: Alert and Notification

This module generates alerts when potentially dangerous close approaches are detected. Notifications include object IDs, estimated approach times, separation distances, and risk categories.

Module 6: Admin Dashboard

The dashboard displays total tracked objects, active satellites, identified debris, object classifications, orbital visualizations, and collision-risk alerts.

8. System Architecture

Orbital Data Sources

9. Working Process

  1. Collect orbital data from available satellite tracking sources.
  2. Process and store the collected information.
  3. Use AI to classify different orbital objects.
  4. Calculate estimated satellite and debris positions.
  5. Display orbital movements through a 3D Earth model.
  6. Compare predicted positions to identify close approaches.
  7. Generate collision-risk alerts.
  8. Display object details and monitoring results on the dashboard.

10. Advantages

  • Provides centralized space debris monitoring.
  • Supports AI-based object classification.
  • Displays orbital movements in 3D.
  • Identifies potentially dangerous close approaches.
  • Generates automated monitoring alerts.
  • Reduces manual data analysis efforts.
  • Supports space research and satellite safety.
  • Can be expanded with additional datasets and features.

11. Applications

  • Space research organizations.
  • Satellite operating companies.
  • Aerospace engineering institutions.
  • Space traffic management.
  • Educational institutions.
  • Space sustainability research.
  • Satellite monitoring programs.

12. Future Enhancements

  • Integration with additional real-time orbital datasets.
  • Improved AI classification accuracy.
  • Advanced collision probability estimation.
  • Mobile application development.
  • Historical space debris analysis.
  • Automated monitoring reports.
  • Integration with space debris removal mission-planning simulations.

13. Expected Outcome

The expected outcome is an intelligent web-based application that identifies and classifies orbital objects, tracks their movements, visualizes satellite orbits, and estimates potential collision risks.

Users can explore a 3D Earth model, view tracked objects, monitor their orbital paths, and receive alerts about potentially dangerous close approaches.

14. Conclusion

Orbit Guard is an innovative project that combines Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, orbital mechanics, and data visualization to address the growing problem of space debris. It provides an intelligent platform for detecting orbital objects, monitoring their movements, and estimating potential collision risks. Through its interactive dashboard and automated alert system, the project supports better space awareness and safer satellite operations.

Orbit Guard aims to contribute to a cleaner, safer, and more sustainable space environment for future generations.

15. Reference Websites

  • CelesTrak  – Satellite orbital datasets.
  • Space-Track  – Space object tracking information.
  • NASA  – Space research and orbital debris information.
  • European Space Agency  – Space debris research.

Recommended hackathon demonstration: Show an orbital object being detected, classified by AI, displayed on a 3D Earth, and monitored for a potential close approach. This will demonstrate the complete working concept of OrbitGuard.
